name: Swiss Cheese Fondue
description: Swiss cheese fondue depends on real technique at every step - the pot is rubbed with a cut garlic clove first (then discarded), the cheese is tossed with real cornstarch before melting to keep it smooth rather than clumping, and once the cheese starts melting into the wine, real tradition never stops stirring, working the spoon in a continuous figure-8 pattern to keep it silky.

steps_detailed: Rub the inside of a heavy pot with the cut side of the garlic, then discard it.
Toss the shredded cheeses with the cornstarch until well coated - real technique depends on this to keep the fondue smooth.
Warm the wine in the pot until it just begins to simmer.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, stirring continuously in a figure-8 pattern and letting each addition melt before adding the next - never stop stirring.
Serve immediately with the bread cubes for dipping.

name: Swiss Rösti
description: Rösti, whose name genuinely means 'crisp and golden', depends on real technique that starts well before frying - the potatoes are parboiled whole first, then cooled completely (even overnight), and only then shredded and pan-fried, which is what keeps the inside tender while the outside turns properly crisp.
steps_detailed: Parboil the whole, unpeeled potatoes 12-15 minutes, until just barely tender - not fully cooked through.
Drain and let cool completely, ideally refrigerated for a few hours or overnight - real technique depends on this real cooling step.
Shred the cooled potatoes coarsely.
Melt the butter in a pan, add the shredded potato, season with salt, and press into an even disc.
Cook over medium heat, undisturbed, 8-10 minutes per side, until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Swiss Älplermagronen
description: Älplermagronen, meaning 'herdsman's macaroni', is a real layered dish of pasta, potato, and cheese baked together, real technique served with real applesauce alongside, a genuine sweet-savory pairing, not an odd addition.
steps_detailed: Boil the pasta and potato together until both are tender, 10-12 minutes.
Fry the onion separately, 8-9 minutes, until deeply golden.
Toss the pasta and potato with the cream and cheese while still hot.
Top with the fried onion - real tradition serves this with applesauce alongside.

name: Swiss Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and dill, reflecting Switzerland's real Alpine lake fishing tradition.

Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
